answer: The network runs five interview waves each epoch. In every wave, each key is paired with a random juror on a private whisper channel and has 40 seconds to answer follow-ups built from its previous sentence. All keys are called together, so one operator cannot drive two seats. A shared script dissolves across an ocean of clones once the questions diverge. Each pass is cut into a public marble register for that key; miss two waves and payouts freeze. Five exclusive live seats per key means 90 added fakes need 90 added operators in lockstep — labor that will not fit on one keyboard.
